answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
Potential benefits:
• Greater transparency and accuracy in assessing the real climate impact of projects and investments.
• Incentive for renewable projects in high-carbon-intensity regions.
• Alignment with long-term decarbonization policies.

Challenges and unintended consequences (especially in the Brazilian context):
• Operational complexity: The Brazilian National Interconnected System (SIN) is highly interconnected, with centralized dispatch by the National System Operator (ONS). Consequential methods based on hourly and regional granularity may not reflect the physical reality of the system.
• High costs: Requirements for geographic and hourly matching (24/7) would increase CAPEX and OPEX, especially for storage and flexibility.
• Market distortion: Could devalue existing renewable assets and restrict the commercialization of PPAs and RECs between submarkets.
• Lack of granular data: Hourly marginal emission data is not widely available or validated in Brazil.
• Risk of double counting: If not harmonized with attributional methods (Scope 2).

answers.label: Appropriateness of the TWG subgroup formula
Why the formula is or is not appropriate
answers.text: The proposed formula is overly simplified and does not capture the complexity of the Brazilian National Interconnected System (SIN). It assumes the availability of hourly marginal emission data, which is not representative in a system with centralized dispatch and high participation of hydroelectric plants (which act as systemic storage). Furthermore, it ignores the role of renewable sources in reducing the system’s average and marginal emissions over time.

answers.label: Secondary effects to consider, and how
answers.text:
The following should be considered:
• Emissions avoided due to hydroelectric flexibility: Hydro plants enable the integration of wind and solar, reducing the need for thermal generation.
• Grid expansion impacts: Renewable projects can defer investments in transmission and fossil generation.
• Lifecycle emissions (construction, decommissioning): Should be included if they represent more than 5% of the primary impact.
• Methodology: Use Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) factors and system expansion modeling (e.g., ONS’s Ten-Year Expansion Plan).

answers.label: Annual versus lifetime impact reporting
selections: Reported once for the lifetime of the project

answers.label: Why annual or lifetime reporting
answers.text: The climate impact of a renewable project is a cumulative result over its lifetime. Annual reporting introduces accounting noise and does not reflect real additionality. Moreover, in Brazil, PPA and REC contracts are long-term (20+ years), and a single assessment provides greater predictability and security for investors and buyers.

answers.label: Requiredness of the financial analysis test
Requiredness of the common practice test
Why selected tests should be included
answers.text: • Contractual/tenor test: Long-term PPAs provide the financial certainty needed for the construction of new projects, especially in emerging markets

answers.label: Context on test feasibility
answers.text: In Brazil, policy-based tests (regulatory) are less relevant due to regulatory stability. Financial tests are difficult to audit. The contract test (PPA) is widely used and verifiable.

answers.label: Additionality tests missing from the framework
answers.text: • Systemic impact test: Assesses whether the project contributes to reducing the system’s average emissions (e.g., hydroelectric plants as enablers of variable renewables).

answers.label: Regions warranting different tests, with examples
answers.text:
• Brazil (SIN): Policy-based tests are less relevant; contract (PPA) and common practice tests are more appropriate.
• Europe/USA: Regulatory and financial tests are more applicable due to mature markets and specific policies.

answers.label: Why that temporal granularity ceiling
answers.text: Hourly granularity is technically possible, but in Brazil it should be used with caution due to the predominance of hydroelectric plants (which have seasonal, not hourly, dispatch). Annual data is sufficient for most applications.

answers.label: Research supporting the suggested approach
answers.text:
• Ten-Year Expansion Plan (PDE) – ONS
• CO2 Emission Factor Studies – MCTI
• SEEG Reports (System of Estimates of Greenhouse Gas Emissions)
